cards.text: The time of Moses' death is near (Deuteronomy 31:14), and he recites a song to the whole assembly of Israel, from beginning to end. He opens by calling on the heavens and the earth to listen. Friend, when your first line is addressed to the SKY, everybody in the room sits up straight.

cards.question: Moses wants his teaching to land soft, the way something settles on new grass. What does he want his words to be like?

cards.text: Then he says why he's singing: he will proclaim the name of the LORD. And he gives God a name that's SOLID. Doesn't move, doesn't crack, nothing like my edges back in the drawer.

cards.question: Moses calls God the ___, a name that shows up again and again in this song.

cards.text: His work is perfect, and all His ways are just. But then the song turns: His people have acted corruptly toward Him, a perverse and crooked generation.

cards.question: Moses asks if this is how they repay the LORD. What does he say the LORD is to them?

cards.text: So Moses says: remember the days of old, and ask your father and your elders, and they'll tell you. Friend, nobody has to ask ME twice. I've got YEARS of junk drawer stories ready to go.
Here's what they'd hear. When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance and set the boundaries of the peoples, the LORD had a portion of His own.

cards.question: Out of all the nations, Moses says the LORD's own portion is His people, Jacob.
Moses goes back to where it all started. Where did the LORD first find Jacob?

cards.text: There He surrounded him, instructed him and guarded him as the apple of His eye. Then Moses paints a picture: an eagle stirring up its nest and hovering over its young.

cards.question: In Moses' picture, the LORD is like that eagle. He spread His ___ to catch them.
Moses says the LORD had help from foreign gods when He led His people.

cards.text: And He fed them: milk, curds, the fat of lambs, the choicest wheat, the finest grapes. Plus honey from the LAST place you'd ever look, like opening a junk drawer and finding a warm batch of cookies.

cards.question: Where does the honey come from in Moses' song?

cards.text: Then Jeshurun, which is another name for Israel (Isaiah 44:1-2), grew fat and kicked. Bloated and gorged, like me after one too many test batches, except I don't kick, I just lie there on my gold base and groan.

cards.question: Full and comfortable, Jeshurun ___ the God who made him.

cards.text: Honey from a ROCK, and they went looking for other gods. They provoked God's jealousy with foreign gods and enraged Him with abominations.

cards.question: Moses says Israel sacrificed, but not to God. Who did they sacrifice to?
The gods Israel turned to were old gods their fathers had always feared.
Moses tells them they ignored the ___ who brought them forth and forgot the God who gave them birth.

cards.text: When the LORD saw this, He rejected them, provoked to anger by His own sons and daughters. Then the LORD Himself speaks.

cards.question: The LORD says He will hide His face from His people.

cards.text: He calls them children of unfaithfulness. They made Him jealous with what is not God, with worthless idols, so He turns it right back around on them.

cards.question: Israel made God jealous with what is not God. How does God say He'll make them jealous?

answers.text: By those who aren't even a people
By those who lead His own people
By those who serve at His altar

cards.text: His anger is a fire that burns to the depths of Sheol. He'll heap disasters on them: hunger, plague, wild beasts and vipers.

cards.question: In the song, the sword and the terror spare the infant and the gray-haired man.

cards.text: Then God says He would have said He'd cut them to pieces and blot out their memory from mankind. But there's an if.

cards.question: What held God back from blotting out the memory of His people?

answers.text: Their enemies would take the credit
Moses would beg Him to stop
Israel would turn back to Him

cards.text: Moses says Israel has no understanding, and if only they were wise, they'd see where this is heading. Then he asks: how could one man chase a THOUSAND, or two put ten thousand to flight?

cards.question: One man chasing a thousand. What does Moses say is the only way that could happen?

answers.text: The LORD had given them up
Their army had grown too small
Their weapons had grown too old

cards.question: Moses says even the enemies admit that their rock is not like Israel's Rock.

cards.text: Then the song turns to vines: their vine is from the vine of Sodom and the fields of Gomorrah. Friend, that is NOT a vineyard you put on the label.

cards.question: What are the grapes from that vine like?

cards.text: Then God speaks again, and friend, He is NOT scrambling: "Have I not stored up these things, sealed up within My vaults?" Meanwhile I can't find my spare timer, and my bakery has ONE room.

cards.question: In the song, who does God say vengeance belongs to?

cards.text: Their foot will slip, and their doom is coming quickly. And then, right there, the song turns toward hope: the LORD will vindicate His people.

cards.question: The LORD will have compassion on His servants. When?

answers.text: When He sees their strength is gone
When they win their next battle
When they bring a bigger offering

cards.text: God asks where their gods are now, the ones that ate the fat of their sacrifices: let them rise up and help! I picture them like the dead batteries I shared that junk drawer with, swearing they've STILL got a little charge left.

cards.question: God says there are other gods besides Him, but He is the greatest.
God brings death and gives life, and He wounds and heals. He says there is ___ who can deliver from His hand.

cards.text: Then God lifts up His hand to heaven and makes a declaration. Friend, when GOD raises His hand to declare something, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: When God lifts His hand to heaven and declares, what does He swear by?

cards.text: He'll sharpen His flashing sword and repay those who hate Him. And then the song ends with a call to rejoice.

cards.question: At the end of the song, who does Moses call to rejoice with God's people?

cards.text: Moses calls the heavens to rejoice and all God's angels to worship Him, because He will cleanse His land and His people. That's the whole song, friend, but this story isn't done yet, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answers "In a crowded city" and "In a fertile valley" are generic places, not real details from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The question says God "swear[s] by" something, but Deuteronomy 32:40 says He lifts His hand to heaven and "declare[s]: As surely as I live forever." The text never calls it swearing. Card 13 also calls it a declaration, so the two cards don't match.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says the heavens rejoice and the angels worship "because He will cleanse His land and His people." In Deuteronomy 32:43 the only "for" is "for He will avenge the blood of His children," and it follows the call to the nations. The cleansing is never given as the reason for the heavens' rejoicing, so the card adds a reason and a connection the text doesn't make.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This is the second fill in the blank with "Rock" as the answer, and Stop 3 card 3 asks about the Rock again. Stop 1 card 4 already asked it and told the baker the name "shows up again and again in this song," so this card tests almost nothing new. The refrain rule covers a repeated line, not a repeated name or title in different lines.
findings.question: When a key name or title (like "Rock") repeats across different lines of a passage, can it be the answer on more than one choice card, or should it be asked only the first time it appears, like a refrain?
